title: Board review of medical-emergency deviation prescriptions and the Drug Store reach of 247 CMR 9.05
subtopic: Reach of the Board's interchangeable drugs regulation
rule_summary: 247 CMR 9.05(1)(b), after requiring that in the instances described in 247 CMR 9.05(1)(a) the pharmacist record the date, hour and nature of the medical emergency on the back of the prescription or in the computerized pharmacy system and that the person purchasing the drug product indicate acceptance of this deviation from the law in writing, provides that all such prescriptions shall be clearly identifiable and available for review by the Board. 247 CMR 9.05(3)(e), lettered as the last item of the labeling paragraph, provides that 247 CMR 9.05 shall only apply to prescriptions dispensed by a pharmacy with a Drug Store Pharmacy License.
exam_relevance: Tests that a prescription filled under the medical-emergency deviation must be clearly identifiable and available for Board review in addition to the emergency record and the purchaser's written acceptance, and that by its words 247 CMR 9.05 reaches prescriptions dispensed by a pharmacy with a Drug Store Pharmacy License.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy, interchangeable drugs

common_confusions: Treating the emergency record and the purchaser's written acceptance as all that 247 CMR 9.05(1)(b) asks. The prescriptions shall also be clearly identifiable and available for review by the Board.
Overlooking 247 CMR 9.05(3)(e) because it is lettered under the labeling paragraph. Its words refer to 247 CMR 9.05.
verification_notes: Read in the current 247 CMR 9.00 published on mass.gov (page footers dated 12/6/24) on 2026-09-16.
